subject: Private Endpoint outbound governance and ephemeral NAT contingency
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@atlashealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Atlas Health Security <sec-compliance@atlashealth.com>, Procurement <procure@atlashealth.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Allowlist + NAT rotation question for private endpoint deployment

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Two items surfaced from our security and procurement teams that I need documented before we proceed: 1) an allowlist (IPs/FQDNs) that our perimeter firewall can use for outbound egress to Redwood control and runtime endpoints, and 2) whether Redwood supports an architecture where the runtime egress IPs are ephemeral (rotating / short-lived) while the control plane and audit traffic come from a static, customer-allowlistable set.

Our security policy requires explicit evidence that ephemeral egress won't break telemetry, audit logs, or license metering. If ephemeral IPs are supported, we also need an attestation/process that ties requests to a stable tenant identity (e.g., mTLS client certs, signed JWTs, or a short-lived origin assertion).

Attached is a short template of what our firewall team expects for allowlist entries. Can you confirm the practical firewall rules (ports/FQDNs/IPs), how we signal tenant identity for ephemeral flows, and whether Redwood can provide a temporary stand-in static egress (proxy) during rollout if needed?

Best,
Samantha

Samantha Lee
Head of Cloud Security, Atlas Health
Samantha.Lee@atlashealth.com

Subject: Re: Allowlist + NAT rotation question for private endpoint deployment

Samantha — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Laura (networking/console) and David (runtime infra) to respond with a concise proposal. High level answer: yes, we can support ephemeral runtime egress while preserving tenant identity and auditability. We typically provide three options and can operate a hybrid during transition:

- Option A (Default): Static egress for both control and runtime — simplest for customer firewalls (we provide small set of stable IPs + FQDNs).
- Option B (Hybrid): Control plane uses static IPs/FQDNs (for onboarding, config, metrics) while runtime tokenized/mTLS flows egress via ephemeral NATs. Tenant identity is asserted via mTLS client certs and a signed origin assertion that's included in the request headers. Monitoring / billing uses signed tokens + request IDs so we can correlate events.
- Option C (Proxy-assisted): Customer routes runtime outbound to a customer-managed or partner proxy with static egress; Redwood verifies origin via mTLS/JWT. Good for strict allowlist-only environments.

David will include the exact ports, FQDNs, and an example attest flow. Laura has a sample runbook we can add to your drive. If helpful, we can stand up a temporary static-proxy endpoint (30-day) for your initial rollout while you validate policies.

I'll attach a short diagram and a runbook stub.

—Markus

Markus Klein
VP, Product Operations | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com
Attachment: ephemeral-nat-design-v1.svg, runbook-egress-samples.txt

From: david_kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@atlashealth.com>
Cc: markus.klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, laura.bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Allowlist + NAT rotation question for private endpoint deployment

Samantha — technical details below (concise checklist for your firewall/opns team). Happy to hop on a 30-minute call to walk through rules.

Required outbound egress (recommended):
- Control plane (static, required for console, billing, alerts):
  - IPs: 54.243.12.80/32, 3.130.98.21/32 (we'll provide final list in signed manifest during kickoff)
  - Ports: TCP 443 (HTTPS), TCP 5222 for internal telemetry (optional; we tunnel telemetry over TLS 443 by default)
  - FQDNs: control.redwood-inference.com, console.redwood-inference.com

- Runtime inference egress (ephemeral paths allowed):
  - Ports: TCP 443 only (TLS enforced).
  - FQDNs: runtime.redwood-inference.com (SNI required), cache.redwood-inference.com (optional for prefix caching).
  - Ephemeral IP behavior: runtime workers egress from ephemeral NAT pools owned by Redwood in your region. IPs rotate; we provide a signed IP manifest (daily) and an attest header on each request: X-Redwood-Origin: base64(signed-assertion).

Tenant identity & audit correlation (how we keep audits intact with ephemeral IPs):
- mTLS: We support mutual TLS for customer control plane connections and can provision a tenant client cert for your control plane to authenticate.
- Signed assertions: Each inference request includes a short-lived signed JWT (<= 2m validity) that contains tenant_id, request_id, timestamp, and routing_hint. Redwood's runtime verifies the JWT and logs it with request traces.
- Request provenance: Every tokenized request is recorded with request_id and retained in audit logs (retention configurable as part of Private deployment).

Firewall guidance (sample ACL rules):
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to control.redwood-inference.com and runtime.redwood-inference.com (SNI enforcement recommended).
- Block outbound to raw IPs except the control plane block we provide. Use FQDN-based allowlist for runtime to allow ephemeral NAT ranges to change.
- DNS: Allow outbound DNS to your recursive resolvers. We recommend split-horizon DNS for private deployments if you use internal FQDNs.

Operational fallbacks:
- Temporary static egress proxy: we can provide a static-proxy fronting runtime traffic for 30 days (static IPs) while you validate observability and telemetry correlation.
- Emergency failover: If a packet is rejected due to an unknown ephemeral IP, logs will include request_id and signed-assertion; we can replay traces for the exact timeframe.

Attachments included: example runbook snippets (runbook-egress-samples.txt) with ip match rules and sample curl commands showing signed-assertion header.

Let me know if you want the manifest frequency changed from daily to hourly.

-David

David Kim
Senior Systems Architect, Runtime Infrastructure
Attachment: runbook-egress-samples.txt

Thanks Markus/David — that level of detail helps a lot. Our security team reviewed the proposed hybrid model (Option B) and is comfortable with the signed-assertion + mTLS combination, provided we have:

- A signed IP manifest delivered daily (hourly preferred for production).
- An initial 14-day static-proxy window during rollout (we'll need the static IPs first thing next week).
- A sample audit replay demonstrating correlation between request_id and billing records.

Procurement is looping in legal to add a short SOW amendment for the static-proxy window and manifest SLA. Can you confirm you can provide the static-proxy IPs by Monday 2025-06-23? Also please add the DocuSign link for the SOW amendment when available.

Samantha
